name: Test-only cycle

lead: A test-only cycle means a course of testosterone as the only anabolic steroid, without other compounds added. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing circles it is often called the baseline or beginner approach, aimed at more muscle, a fuller physique and, in some posts, secondary effects on the face.

Testosterone activates androgen receptors and promotes muscle growth and maintenance. Forum users disagree about its appearance trade-offs, with some calling it all that is needed and others arguing it brings aging, hair-loss and skin effects.

paras: Users describe it in general terms as an injected testosterone ester taken for a number of weeks, sometimes paired with hair-loss or other support products. Dosing and sourcing are not covered here.

Documented effects include acne, oily skin, scalp hair loss in predisposed people, suppression of natural testosterone and sperm production, raised blood pressure and unfavourable cholesterol changes, and cardiovascular concerns. Testosterone is a controlled substance (US Schedule III, UK Class C) and is on the WADA prohibited list.

angle.text: Testosterone raises androgen levels, which promotes muscle growth and maintenance. Users use a test-only course to build a bigger physique, while discussing trade-offs in hair, skin and face.

lead: A test-only cycle is a period of non-medical testosterone use in which no other anabolic-androgenic steroid is added. On looksmax.org it is discussed as the standard entry point for people seeking more muscle, with threads such as one titled "All you need is a test only cycle" and others asking whether it helps facial bone mass or hair loss.[1][2][3]

Testosterone is the reference androgen: through androgen receptor activation it supports muscle growth and maintenance, and it also acts on skin, hair and fertility.[4][5] Injectable esters are the usual non-medical route because oral testosterone is largely inactivated before reaching circulation.[5]

Opinion on the appearance outcome is divided. One looksmax.org thread argues testosterone is "unselective" and yields aging, hair loss and skin effects for modest muscle, while other posts present it as sufficient.[2][3]
infobox: US Schedule III, UK Class C, Canada Schedule IV[4]

paras: The term describes testosterone used on its own rather than "stacked" with other steroids. Testosterone esters act as prodrugs releasing the hormone over time, and intramuscular injection is the most common route.[4]

Posters on looksmax.org ask whether a test-only course can build facial bone mass, whether it causes hair loss, and whether it is enough on its own.[1][3][6] Replies range from telling a tall 18-year-old he does not need it to arguing the opposite view that testosterone is the worst choice for looks, with SARMs or more tissue-selective compounds preferred.[1][2]

Reviews list acne, oily skin, stretch marks, fluid retention, accelerated pattern baldness in predisposed men via DHT, suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis with reduced sperm production, gynecomastia, raised LDL and lowered HDL cholesterol, hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy.[4][5] The FDA changed testosterone labelling in February 2025, adding a blood pressure warning.[5]

Testosterone is Schedule III in the US, Class C in the UK and Schedule IV in Canada, prescription-only in the EU, and on the WADA list.[5] A black market of smuggled or counterfeit products exists in regulated markets.[4]
No studies found of the "test-only cycle" as practised in these communities. Related research covers medical testosterone replacement.[5]

lore.intro: Test-only cycles are widely debated on looksmax.org as a baseline, with disagreement about benefits versus aging and hair effects.[1][2][3]
